sources.title: Definition of the hydrogen bond (IUPAC Recommendations 2011)
sources.retrieval: Direct initial URL returned403; primary search result subsequently opened successfully as parsed full5-page PDF, printed1637–1641,136 text lines.
sources.reviewed_scope: Definition section2, donor/acceptor descriptions, criteriaE1–E3 and footnotesF2/F4.
sources.confirmation: Water O–H donors and electron-rich O acceptors support the selected intermolecular example. Definition is broader than an exclusively electrostatic or fixed-element school mnemonic; the draft does not claim that mnemonic universally or rank all interaction energies. No figure copied.

sources.title: IUPAC Gold Book: van der Waals forces
sources.retrieval: Direct HTML/PDF opens403; primary-indexed full short entry retrieved by search, including definition, included force components and sourcecitation.
sources.confirmation: London dispersion is an included component, not a synonym for every covalent or hydrogen interaction. The draft's wording is compatible with this restricted claim.

sources.title: OpenStax Chemistry2e10.1 Intermolecular Forces
sources.retrieval: Primary publisher page retrieved,245 lines; force distinctions/dispersion and water discussion read.
sources.confirmation: Molecules remain distinct from intermolecular cohesion in ordinary boiling; dispersion applies broadly and grows with polarizability/geometry. I2 is a molecular solid with dispersion, unlike the internal I–I bond. The draft avoids treating all dispersion as weaker than every hydrogen bond.

sources.title: OpenStax Chemistry2e7.3 Lewis Symbols and Structures
sources.confirmation: Valence-electron bookkeeping, sharing and lone-pair Lewis representations provide the level of model used; origins of dots/crosses do not make distinct electron species. Independent electron/charge solutions retained separately.

sources.title: OpenStax Chemistry2e10.5 The Solid State of Matter
sources.retrieval: Primary publisher page retrieved,140 lines; ionic,metallic,covalent-network and molecular sections read.
sources.confirmation: Four structure classes, ionic carrier mobility and network exceptions match the draft. Graphite's layered exception is retained. If teaching carbon phase transitions quantitatively, distinguish ambient-pressure sublimation from pressure-dependent melting; no carbon melting procedure or numeric temperature is supplied by the draft.

sources.title: RSC Carbon — properties and uses
sources.retrieval: Primary organisation page retrieved; factbox and properties/uses sections read.
sources.confirmation: Carbon allotropes differ in structure and properties; graphite marking/electrical brush use and diamond cutting use support the supplied jobs. Carbon factbox describes sublimation; no ordinary-pressure molten-carbon claim should be added.

sources.title: RSC Aluminium — properties and uses
sources.retrieval: Primary organisation page retrieved; factbox,properties/uses and protective-oxide transcript paragraph read.
sources.confirmation: About660C melting,low density,malleability,electrical/thermal conduction and protective oxide are supported. Only these material facts were used; health/podcast speculation,prices and universal product-safety claims were not adopted. Manufacturer instructions remain absent and required for actual product advice.
